get.description: Whether the API is up. No key needed. Does not use credits.

post.description: Start a device login, for a machine with no browser. Show the person verification_uri_complete and user_code, then poll POST /auth/token every interval seconds. No key needed. Does not use credits.

post.description: The key in the Authorization header revokes itself, as revcenter auth logout does. Answers revoked: false for a key that is already revoked or unknown. Does not use credits.

Trade a sign-in for a key, returned once. A browser sign-in sends grant_type authorization_code with the code from the loopback redirect, its PKCE code_verifier and the same redirect_uri. A device login polls with device_code: authorization_pending (or slow_down) until someone authorizes it at /oauth/device. Errors: access_denied, expired_token, invalid_grant. No key needed. Does not use credits.

grant_type.description: authorization_code for a browser sign-in; omit (or device_code) to poll a device login.

code.description: The rvca_ code the browser brought to redirect_uri.

code_verifier.description: The PKCE verifier whose S256 challenge opened /oauth/authorize.

redirect_uri.description: The loopback address the code was sent to, exactly.

get.description:
How busy Revcenter is right now: searches running and waiting across the platform and in this workspace, and about when a search launched now would start. Launches are never refused for being busy: a search past the platform's limit waits its turn (status queued) and starts as one finishes. Workspaces take turns, so a workspace with many searches waiting does not hold up another's first one. Use this to tell the person what to expect before launching many searches at once. Does not use credits.

Needs scope `searches:read`.

post.description:
What an action would do and spend, without doing it; returns a proposal_id that apply_proposal runs within 30 minutes. Works for every action marked proposable in GET /actions. Previewing a requirement change re-scores nothing until it is applied, except that its before/after is computed on the people already read. Previewing launch_search with criteria returns compiled_query: the exact titles, keyword terms, locations, level, years and employers the search will send. page_one_estimate is null in a preview (reading page 1 is paid); the search records it once it runs. Does not use credits.

Needs scope `searches:read`.

post.description:
Start a LinkedIn search in a project, on `criteria` run exactly as sent, or on a `jd_text` Revcenter reads; with database_only it scores the workspace's candidates on file and uses no credits. Send an Idempotency-Key: a retry with the same key, project and body returns the same search; the same key on a different request returns 409 idempotency_key_reused. max_credits (250 to 20,000, default 1,000; below 250 is refused with 400 max_credits_too_low, as a smaller cap cannot buy one page of results and read it) is reserved at launch and refused with 402 shortlist_allocation_exhausted when the workspace can't cover it; when the search finishes it is charged for the profiles it read, never more than max_credits, and the rest comes back (get_search credits_charged). A search that fails is refunded in full. Reserves up to max_credits credits (1,000 by default); unused credits are refunded.

Needs scope `searches:write`.

jd_text.description: A job description, when not sending criteria.

database_only.description: Search only the workspace's candidates on file. Uses no credits.

max_credits.description: The most this search may use, in credits: reserved now, charged for the profiles it reads, and the rest refunded when it finishes. At least 250: a smaller cap can't buy one page of results and read it. Presets 500, 1000, 2500, 5000.

get.summary: List every record a search returned
get.description:
Every person a search's result pages listed, read or not, in the order returned: each with what became of them (scored, known, not_read), the score if scored, and the read profile when this workspace holds one. list_people and the shortlist hold only the people a search scored; this is everyone it found, one record per person (the page that listed them first wins). scored: read and scored in this search. known: already in this workspace from another search, so not read again. not_read: listed but never read (screened out, left for a later round, or the search stopped). candidate_id and profile are null for people this workspace has not read. A database-only search returns no records. For every search in a project at once, use list_project_records; for everyone across the workspace, list_candidates. No contact details. Does not use credits.

Needs scope `shortlists:read`.

get.summary: Download every record a search returned as CSV
get.description:
Every record a search returned as CSV, one row per person in the order returned: status, score, page, name, title, company, location, LinkedIn address, summary and headline, and the read profile's experience, education and skills as text columns and as numbered columns; or as JSON Lines with format=jsonl. Columns after candidate_id: headline, about, experience_history, education, skills, certifications, languages, projects, connections, then the career as numbered columns (experience_1_title, experience_1_company, experience_1_location, experience_1_start, experience_1_end, experience_1_months, experience_1_description … experience_10_*, education_1_school, education_1_degree, education_1_field, education_1_start, education_1_end … education_5_*, total_experience_months, current_role_months). UTF-8 with a byte order mark, so Excel reads it as written. ?format=jsonl returns JSON Lines instead: one person per line with the whole read profile, lossless; for an AI agent, JSONL; CSV is for spreadsheets. Does not use credits.

Needs scope `shortlists:read`.

parameters.description: csv (the default) for a spreadsheet, with a UTF-8 byte order mark; jsonl for JSON Lines: one person per line with the whole read profile, lossless, for an AI agent

get.summary: List every record a project's searches returned
get.description:
Every person any of a project's searches returned, expansions included, once each in the order returned: status rolled up across the searches (scored, known, not_read), the best score, which searches returned them, and the read profile when this workspace holds one. One record per person across the project (the earliest listing wins), with the same fields as list_search_records plus first_search_id (the search that listed them first) and search_ids (every search in the project that returned them). status is scored when any of the project's searches scored them, else known when this workspace already holds them, else not_read; score is the best any of the project's searches gave. For everyone across the whole workspace, use list_candidates. No contact details. Does not use credits.

Needs scope `shortlists:read`.

code.description: Stable: every code is on the Errors page.

device_code.description: Secret: send it to POST /auth/token. Never show it.

user_code.description: Show it; the user checks it matches the page.

verification_uri_complete.description: Open this in the user's browser.

api_key.description: The new key, shown once. Store it; never print it.

search_slots.description: Searches that run at once across the platform.

typical_search_seconds.description: Median time from start to finish of a recent search.

searches_per_hour.description: About how many searches the platform finishes an hour at that pace.

new_search.description: Where a search launched now would stand: 0 seconds when it would start at once.

credits_reserved.description: What applying it reserves; unused credits are refunded when the search finishes.

effect.description: What the action would do: the before/after for a scoring change, capacity and credits for a search.

credits_reserved.description: Credits held for this search: its max_credits, or 0 for database_only.

stop_reason.description: Why it stopped: target_reached, discovery_exhausted (LinkedIn had no more), low_yield, page_cap, budget_exhausted (used its cap), cap_too_small (its cap could not buy one page of results and read it: nothing bought, every credit refunded), cancelled, failed.

queue.description: While the search waits its turn (status queued): its place in line and about how many seconds until it starts. Null otherwise.

credits_reserved.description: Credits held at launch (max_credits); 0 for a database-only search.

credits_charged.description: What the search was charged once it closed, never more than credits_reserved; the rest was refunded. Null while it runs.

fit.description: How the person reads on each criterion (title, location, years, skills…).

profile.description: The full read profile: experience, education, skills, certifications, languages, projects. No contact details.

candidate_id.description: The person's id in this workspace (as list_people, add_shortlist_members); null when this workspace has not read them.

status.description: scored: read and scored in this search. known: already in this workspace from another search. not_read: listed, never read.

page.description: The result page that listed them first.

open_profile.description: Can be messaged without a connection.

profile.description: The full read profile, as list_people gives it; null when not read. No contact details.

allOf.description: status rolls up across the project's searches (scored beats known beats not_read); score is the best any of them gave.

first_search_id.description: The search whose page listed them first.

search_ids.description: Every search in the project that returned them, earliest first.

events.description: Event types it receives, or ["*"] for all.

disabled_reason.description: Why it is off: turned off, or 20 deliveries in a row abandoned.

consecutive_failures.description: Deliveries abandoned in a row; a delivered one resets it.

secret.description: The signing secret (whsec_…), shown once. Verify each delivery's Revcenter-Signature with it.

event_id.description: The same on every retry and redelivery: deduplicate on it.

status.description: failed: the last attempt failed and another is scheduled (next_attempt_at). abandoned: no more attempts.

response_status.description: The HTTP status your endpoint answered; null when it could not be reached.
